criteria: Discussed on Reddit, so acquisition and ORM both apply
Second batch: founder and creator led course brands, smaller than the first ten and far more argued about online, so reputation work is the entry point
meta.email_sourcing: Every address was read off the company's own contact page or rendered site on 2026-09-06 — none pattern-guessed. Re-verify with a validator before sending.
meta.known_gap: These are company inboxes, not decision makers. Pair each with the Head of Marketing / Brand / Growth on LinkedIn; at Scaler, upGrad and TalentSprint (now Accenture) the shared inbox alone will rarely reach anyone with budget. In the creator led batch the founder is the brand, so the shared inbox is more likely to reach someone with authority, but three addresses (GrowthSchool, Booming Bulls, Rachana Ranade) came off indexed pages that block direct reads. Verify those with a validator first.
before_you_send: SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the sending domain
Send from a subdomain (mail.growwdaddy.com), never the root domain that runs the site's own mail
10-15 sends a day, spread out, never a blast
Plain text, no tracking pixel, no attachment, one link at most
Keep the opt-out line — Interview Kickstart is US (CAN-SPAM), upGrad and TalentSprint handle EU learners (GDPR)
meta.email_copy: Approved copy lives in outreach/emails.txt, not here. This file is contacts + sending notes only.

companies.name: Scaler
companies.why_them: The single most-discussed edtech brand on Reddit in India. Sentiment in those threads is doing more selling (or unselling) than any ad.
companies.subject: Scaler on Reddit
companies.body:
Hi Scaler Team,

My name is Shraddha and I work with GrowwDaddy. We run a network of active Reddit users across the communities where people talk about courses, careers and where to spend their money.

I know your programmes get compared a lot by people deciding where to invest in their careers. I wanted to ask if you currently do anything organic on Reddit as part of that?

We help edtech brands source real, motivated people from our network to share genuine reviews and experiences in the threads where those decisions are already being made. It works well for enrolments, and it keeps the conversation around a brand balanced instead of one sided.

If you'd be open to a quick chat, I'd love to connect.

Best,
Shraddha
